audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Fiora all seven stages while the page's own whys say Garen leads level 1, level 2 keeps 'the edge', and levels 3 through 6 are even skill checks. Garen wins 51.76% over 2813 games, and the mirror settled the chart as Level 1 Garen, Levels 2 through First item Skill, 2+ items Fiora.
audit.why: Seven rows conceding a lane the same page says is even-to-favoured early. The mirror already flipped its side; leaving this one would guarantee a mirror conflict.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one group in both layers to Garen / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Fiora, and whys[1] and whys[5] rewritten to argue for a skill phase instead of a Garen lead and a Fiora lead respectively. diffRating to 6.5/10 with the even tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte's cooldown appears once in the full layer as a bare '24s' and nowhere in the content layer, and Lunge's cooldown is never given. Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16 and Lunge is 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6.
audit.why: Riposte's downtime is the entire green-light system in this lane, and Lunge going from 13s to 6s across ranks is why her first-item window feels so different from level 3.
audit.corrected: Riposte quoted as 24s at rank 1 in whys[1], spikes[0] and report[5]; Lunge's drop to 6s at rank 5 in spikes[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: The biggest interaction on the page is stated backwards. Five fields warn about 'her Riposte stun' and 'spinning into her riposte stun'. Riot's text: the stab slows the first champion hit, OR stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with it. Garen's kit contains no immobilizing effect — Decisive Strike silences and slows, Judgment damages, Demacian Justice executes — so against Garen, Riposte can only slow. Separately, three fields call her Vitals 'true damage'; nothing in Riot's description of Duelist's Dance says that, and what it does say (they heal her and grant Move Speed) is the fact that matters.
audit.why: A reader taught to fear a stun plays around a threat that cannot happen in this matchup, and treats the parry as a hard no-go rather than a timed window to bait. The Vitals correction changes the counterplay from resistances to Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: early, spikes[0], report[5] and loading now say Riposte parries all damage and slows, and can only stun if it blocks CC — which Garen does not have. Vitals described by their real effect (healing) in spikes[2], late and wants.foe[1], with Grievous Wounds as the answer in wants.you[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/fiora.json W text, P text, R text

notes: The headline correction: Riposte cannot stun Garen. Riot's text stuns only if the parry blocked an immobilizing effect, and Garen's kit has none — Decisive Strike silences and slows, Judgment damages, Demacian Justice executes. Five fields across both layers warned about a stun that cannot happen in this matchup; the content-layer instances and report[5]/loading are fixed here, but the same wording survives inside the scraped full-layer blocks (tradeGood, breakdown.trading, report[3].t) that are too far outside the band to rewrite. Also dropped the 'true-damage vitals' claim, which Riot's description of Duelist's Dance does not support — the healing is the real effect and Grievous Wounds is the real answer.
